That milky sap is called latex! It acts as a defense against insects and fungal infections, and it also helps seal up the plant's wound.
copy.tl:
Bakit may gatas na lumalabas sa sugat ng ilang halaman?

Ang gatas na iyon ay tinatawag na latex! Ito ay nagsisilbing depensa laban sa mga insekto at fungal na impeksyon, at tumutulong din itong magsara ng sugat ng halaman.
copy.bis:
Ngano naay gatas nga mogawas sa sugat sa uban tanom?

Kanang gatas gitawag og latex! Nagsilbi kini ingong depensa batok sa mga insekto ug fungal nga impeksyon, ug nakatabang usab kini sa pagsira sa sugat sa tanom.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It's Antoine Lavoisier! He earned the title 'Father of Modern Chemistry'.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to identify a famous Filipino and/or foreign scientist and their invention/s
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies a famous foreign scientist (Lavoisier) but does not mention any invention or discovery, which is a required part of the competency. It only gives his title, so it does not directly support the skill of identifying a scientist and their invention.

copy.en:
Who is known as the 'Father of Modern Chemistry'?

It's Antoine Lavoisier! He earned the title 'Father of Modern Chemistry'.
copy.tl:
Sino ang tinaguriang 'Ama ng Modernong Kimika' (Father of Modern Chemistry)?

Si Antoine Lavoisier! Siya ang tinaguriang 'Ama ng Modernong Kimika' (Father of Modern Chemistry).
copy.bis:
Kinsa ang gitawag nga 'Amahan sa Modernong Chemistry'?

Si Antoine Lavoisier! Siya ang gitawag nga 'Amahan sa Modernong Chemistry'.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Lead sinks in water because its density (11.3 g/cm³) is far higher than water's!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe things that affect the movement of objects, including size, shape, heaviness, material, and surface texture
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains sinking via density, but the competency requires exploring/describing factors that affect movement such as size, shape, heaviness, material, and surface texture. Density is not one of the listed factors, and the card does not address any of them directly.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Lead sinks in water because its density (11.3 g/cm³) is far higher than water's!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe matter as anything that has mass and takes up space
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses density, which relates to mass and volume, but it does not describe matter as anything that has mass and takes up space. It does not directly teach the definition of matter or the concept of mass/volume as properties of matter.

copy.en: Lead sinks in water because its density (11.3 g/cm³) is far higher than water's! It drops straight down like a rock.
copy.tl: Lumulubog ang tingga (lead) sa tubig dahil mas mataas ang densidad nito (11.3 g/cm³) kaysa tubig! Tumama siya sa ilalim.
copy.bis: Molunod ang tingga (lead) sa tubig kay mas taas kaayo ang density niini (11.3 g/cm³) kaysa tubig! Modiretso siya sa ubos.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the smaller male has wings to fly off and find a mate
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: differentiate sexual from asexual reproduction in terms of: a) number of parents involved, and b) similarities of offspring to parents
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions mating behavior but does not differentiate sexual from asexual reproduction by number of parents or offspring similarity, which are the required criteria.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the smaller male has wings to fly off and find a mate
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card touches on reproduction indirectly through mate-finding but does not describe the general characteristic that living things reproduce, grow, or respond.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the female is bigger and heavier and can't fly at all, while the smaller male has wings
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes sexual dimorphism but does not explain how animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage.

copy.en: In many leaf insects, the female is bigger and heavier and can't fly at all, while the smaller male has wings to fly off and find a mate.
copy.tl: Sa maraming leaf insect, mas malaki at mabigat ang babae pero hindi ito makalipad, samantalang ang mas maliit na lalaki ay may pakpak para maghanap ng kapareha.
copy.bis: Sa daghang leaf insect, mas dako ug bug-at ang baye apan dili kini makalupad, samtang ang mas gamay nga laki adunay pako aron mangita og kaparis.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The way veins branch in a leaf
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the branching pattern of leaf veins but does not address the role of leaves, roots, or stems in obtaining water and nutrients from the soil. It is only tangentially related to plant parts.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The way veins branch in a leaf
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the root and shoot system in plants and describe why they are important
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions leaf veins, which are part of the shoot system, but it does not describe the importance of the root or shoot system. It only notes a visual pattern, not function or significance.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The way veins branch in a leaf
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe different science process skills used in performing simple science activities, such as observing, predicting, and measuring using units such as millimeter, centimeter, and meter
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not describe any science process skills such as observing, predicting, or measuring, nor does it involve units. It is a descriptive observation about natural patterns, unrelated to the competency.

copy.en: The way veins branch in a leaf looks a lot like tree branches spreading out, or rivers splitting into streams, one big line dividing again and again, the same pattern seen all over nature.
copy.tl: Ang pagsanga ng mga ugat sa dahon ay kahawig ng pagsanga ng mga puno o paghati ng ilog sa mga sapa, mula sa isang malaking linya, paulit-ulit itong nahahati sa mas maliliit, parehong pattern na makikita sa kalikasan.
copy.bis: Ang pagnga sa mga ugat sa dahon susama sa pagnga sa mga sanga sa kahoy o pagbahin sa suba ngadto sa mga sapa, gikan sa usa ka dako nga linya, balik-balik kining mabahin ngadto sa gagmay, managsama nga sumbanan nga makita sa kinaiyahan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A leaf's veins give it strength so it doesn't tear when strong wind or rain hits
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses leaf veins as providing structural strength against wind and rain, but the competency requires identifying the role of leaves, roots, and stems in getting water and nutrients from the soil. The card does not address water or nutrient uptake, so it only shares the broad topic of plant parts without directly supporting the stated skill.

copy.en: A leaf's veins give it strength so it doesn't tear when strong wind or rain hits — especially useful during storms here in the Philippines!
copy.tl: Ang mga ugat ng dahon ay nagbibigay ng lakas dito para hindi ito agad mapunit kapag hinampas ng malakas na hangin o ulan — lalo na sa mga bagyo dito sa Pilipinas!
copy.bis: Ang mga ugat sa dahon naghatag og kusog niini aron dili dayon magisi kon hampakon sa kusog nga hangin o ulan — ilabi na sa mga bagyo dinhi sa Pilipinas!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A leap year has 366 days, which is one more than the usual 365, and it comes every four years!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about the calendar concept of a leap year, not the general structure of the solar system, major celestial objects, their features, or composition.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A leap year has 366 days, which is one more than the usual 365, and it comes every four years!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a Sun-Earth-Moon system model to demonstrate and explain the observable effects of predictable patterns and events including changes in seasons, changes observed in the patterns of visible star over a year, and solar and lunar eclipses
assignedReviews.reason: A leap year relates to Earth's orbital period around the Sun, but the card does not demonstrate or explain seasons, star patterns, or eclipses using a Sun-Earth-Moon model.

copy.en: A leap year has 366 days, which is one more than the usual 365, and it comes every four years!
copy.tl: Ang taong bisiesto ay may 366 araw, isang dagdag mula sa karaniwang 365, at dumarating kada apat na taon!
copy.bis: Ang bisiesto nga tuig adunay 366 ka adlaw, usa ka dugang sa naandang 365, ug moabot matag upat ka tuig!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An honest investigation reports the surprise!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the steps of a simple science investigation (What is the problem? What materials do you need? What do you need to do? What have you found out/learned?)
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses honesty in reporting unexpected results, which touches on the 'What have you found out/learned?' step of a scientific investigation, but it does not describe the steps of a simple science investigation (problem, materials, procedure, findings). It is related to scientific attitudes rather than directly teaching the competency.

copy.en:
What if your experiment results surprise you?

An honest investigation reports the surprise! Never change the numbers just to match your first guess.
copy.tl:
Paano kung ang resulta ng iyong eksperimento ay nakakagulat?

Ang tapat na imbestigasyon ay isinusulat ang sorpresa! Huwag baguhin ang numero para magtugma sa unang hula.
copy.bis:
Unsa kung ang resulta sa imong eksperimento makapahibulong?

Ang matuod nga imbestigasyon isulat ang sorpresa! Ayaw usba ang numero aron mosibo sa unang huna-huna.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It is very strong, so we use it for shoes and belts.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the physical properties of solid materials, such as hard, shiny, or stretchable
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions that leather is strong, which is a physical property, but the competency asks students to describe physical properties of solid materials such as hard, shiny, or stretchable. The card does not teach the concept of physical properties or provide a description of leather's properties beyond a single adjective; its focus is on leather being a natural material from animal skin and its uses. This is only tangentially related to describing physical properties.

copy.en:
What makes leather great for shoes and bags?

Leather is a natural material made from animal skin like a cow! It is very strong, so we use it for shoes and belts.
copy.tl:
Bakit maganda ang katad para sa sapatos at bag?

Ang katad ay natural na materyales na gawa sa balat ng hayop tulad ng baka! Matibay ito, kaya ginagamit sa sapatos at sinturon.
copy.bis:
Nganong maayo ang katad para sa sapatos ug bag?

Ang katad usa ka natural nga materyales nga hinimo gikan sa panit sa hayop sama sa baka! Lig-on kini, maong gigamit sa sapatos ug bakos.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: helps the plant turn sunlight into food
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the process of photosynthesis and respiration, and identify its raw materials needed and products
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that chlorophyll helps the plant turn sunlight into food. It does not describe the process of photosynthesis or respiration, nor identify raw materials and products, which are the core actions of G8-L-9.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Why are leaves green?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the root and shoot system in plants and describe why they are important
assignedReviews.reason: G4-L-2 is about observing the root and shoot system in plants and describing why they are important. The card discusses leaf color and chlorophyll, not the root/shoot system or their importance. No direct or prerequisite support.

copy.en:
Why are leaves green?

It's all thanks to chlorophyll — the green coloring inside leaves that helps the plant turn sunlight into food.
copy.tl:
Bakit berde ang mga dahon?

Dahil sa chlorophyll — ang berdeng kulay sa loob ng dahon na tumutulong sa halaman na gawing pagkain ang sikat ng araw.
copy.bis:
Nganong berde ang mga dahon?

Tungod sa chlorophyll — ang berdeng kolor sa sulod sa dahon nga makatabang sa tanom paghimo og pagkaon gikan sa adlaw.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: chlorophyll soaks up red and blue light but bounces green light straight back to our eyes
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided science activities to explore and describe sources of light, how it behaves or can be changed, and its uses in everyday situations
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a behavior of light (absorption and reflection) but does not involve guided activities, sources of light, or everyday uses. It is a specific biological explanation of leaf color, not direct support for exploring light sources or how light behaves in the sense of the grade 3 competency.

copy.en:
Why do leaves look green to our eyes?

Leaves look green because chlorophyll soaks up red and blue light but bounces green light straight back to our eyes.
copy.tl:
Bakit berde ang tingin natin sa dahon?

Mukhang berde ang dahon dahil sinisipsip ng chlorophyll ang pula at asul na liwanag, pero ibinabalik nito ang berdeng liwanag sa ating mga mata.
copy.bis:
Nganong lunhaw ang atong tan-aw sa dahon?

Mura'g lunhaw ang dahon kay gisuyop sa chlorophyll ang pula ug asul nga kahayag, apan gipabalik niini ang lunhaw nga kahayag sa atong mata.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: If it comes out clean, the proteins have set and the custard is solid.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in temperature cause matter to change in state, such as solid to liquid to gas
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a doneness test for flan, mentioning protein setting and solid custard, but does not describe how changes in temperature cause matter to change state (solid-liquid-gas). It lacks any explicit temperature-state change instruction, so it only shares the broad topic of matter in daily life.

copy.en: Poke the leche flan with a toothpick to check if it's done! If it comes out clean, the proteins have set and the custard is solid.
copy.tl: Tusukin ang leche flan ng toothpick para malaman kung luto na! Kung lumabas itong malinis, hudyat na nagsiksik na ang protina at solid na ang custard.
copy.bis: Tusoka ang leche flan og toothpick aron mahibal-an kon luto na! Kon mogawas nga limpyo ug dili pilit, timailhan nga ang protina nagahi na ug solid na ang custard.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Its saliva has something that numbs the skin
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card is not an example of mimicry or camouflage as animals changed to better suit their environment.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it doesn't hurt much even if the leech stays attached a long time
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe that living things interact with each other in the natural environment, such as through competition, or predation
assignedReviews.reason: The card is not living things interacting through competition or predation.

copy.en:
Why doesn't a medical leech bite hurt?

Its saliva has something that numbs the skin — so it doesn't hurt much even if the leech stays attached a long time!
copy.tl:
Bakit hindi masakit ang kagat ng linta?

May sangkap sa laway nito na pumapamanhid sa balat — kaya hindi masakit kahit matagal itong nakadikit!
copy.bis:
Nganong dili sakit ang paak sa alimatok?

Ang iyang laway adunay sangkap nga makapamanhid sa panit — mao nga dili sakit bisan dugay kining motapot!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A leech's saliva numbs your skin
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a leech's saliva numbing the skin, which is an adaptation for feeding, but it does not describe how animals have changed to better suit their environment, nor does it mention mimicry, camouflage, or any evolutionary change. It only states a current physiological effect, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A leech's saliva numbs your skin
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The competency is about observing and describing outer body parts of animals (head, legs, wings) and their role in movement and food gathering. The card discusses leech saliva numbing the skin, which is not an outer body part and does not relate to movement or food gathering. It is unrelated to the competency.

copy.en:
Why can't you feel a leech biting you?

A leech's saliva numbs your skin, so most people don't even feel it when it bites!
copy.tl:
Bakit hindi mo namamalayan ang kagat ng linta?

May laway ang linta na nagpapamanhid, kaya madalas hindi nararamdaman ng tao ang kagat nito!
copy.bis:
Ngano dili nimo mabati ang paak sa linta?

Ang linta adunay laway nga nagapamanhid, mao nga sagad dili mabati sa tawo ang paak niini!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A leech has a sucker at each end of its body — that's how it clings on so tightly!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes an outer body part (sucker) of a leech, but its stated role is clinging, not moving or gathering food as required by the competency. It shares the topic of animal body parts but does not directly support the skill of identifying roles for movement or food gathering.

copy.en: A leech has a sucker at each end of its body — that's how it clings on so tightly!
copy.tl: May sucker ang linta sa magkabilang dulo ng katawan nito — kaya nakakakapit ito nang mahigpit!
copy.bis: Ang linta adunay sucker sa duha ka tumoy sa lawas niini — mao nga makakupot kini og hugot!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Legume seeds like mung beans are rich in protein
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a nutritional fact about legume seeds but does not identify or teach the basic needs of living things (air, food, water, shelter). It only tangentially relates to food as a need.

copy.en: Legume seeds like mung beans are rich in protein, which helps build a strong body.
copy.tl: Ang mga buto ng legume tulad ng munggo ay mayaman sa protina na nagpapalakas ng katawan.
copy.bis: Ang mga liso sa legume sama sa munggo dato sa protina nga makapalig-on sa lawas.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: damage the kidneys and liver
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use models, flow charts, diagrams, and simulations to explain how body systems work together, such as digestion and excretion
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a fact about leptospirosis damaging kidneys and liver. It does not use models, flow charts, diagrams, or simulations, nor does it explain how body systems work together. The mention of organs is only tangentially related to the competency's focus on system interactions.

copy.en: If leptospirosis is not treated, it can get worse and damage the kidneys and liver.
copy.tl: Kung hindi maagapan ang leptospirosis, maaari itong lumala at makapinsala sa bato at atay.
copy.bis: Kung dili maatiman ang leptospirosis, mahimo kining mograbe ug makadaot sa kidni ug atay.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Lichens are food for some animals, such as reindeer and caribou in cold places
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the roles of producers, consumers, scavengers, and decomposers in a food web
assignedReviews.reason: Lichens as reindeer food is not the roles of producers, consumers, scavengers, and decomposers in a food web.

copy.en: Lichens are food for some animals, such as reindeer and caribou in cold places.
copy.tl: Ang mga lichen ay pagkain ng ilang hayop, tulad ng reindeer at caribou sa malalamig na lugar.
copy.bis: Ang mga lichen pagkaon sa pipila ka hayop, sama sa reindeer ug caribou sa bugnaw nga mga dapit.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: cyanobacteria make food using sunlight too
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the process of photosynthesis and respiration, and identify its raw materials needed and products
assignedReviews.reason: The card only mentions that cyanobacteria make food using sunlight, which is a vague reference to photosynthesis. It does not describe the process of photosynthesis or respiration, nor identify raw materials and products as required by G8-L-9. The content is about lichen symbiosis, not the detailed photosynthetic process.

copy.en: Some lichens team up with cyanobacteria instead of algae -- and just like algae, cyanobacteria make food using sunlight too.
copy.tl: May mga lichen na gumagamit ng cyanobacteria sa halip ng alga, at ito rin ay gumagawa ng pagkain gamit ang sikat ng araw.
copy.bis: Ang uban lichen mogamit og cyanobacteria imbes og alga, ug kini usab naghimo og pagkaon gamit ang adlaw.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: some are flat and crusty, some look like little leaves, and some look like tiny branches
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card only describes different shapes of lichens. It does not use a table, does not classify living things into the named groups (plants, animals, microorganisms including fungi and bacteria), and does not teach classification based on similar characteristics. Lichen is not explicitly placed in any of the required groups.

copy.en: Lichen can look totally different depending on the type — some are flat and crusty, some look like little leaves, and some look like tiny branches.
copy.tl: Iba't ibang hugis ang lichen — ang iba ay patag at parang kumakapit na balat, ang iba ay parang dahon, at ang iba ay parang maliliit na sanga.
copy.bis: Lainlain ang porma sa lichen — ang uban patag ug morag nagkapyot nga panit, ang uban morag dahon, ug ang uban morag gagmayng sanga.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A dragonfly lays its eggs in water, and its young live underwater as a nymph before climbing out to become a flying dragonfly.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use flow charts to compare the different stages in the life cycle of animals, such as a butterfly, frog, chicken, and human
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the life-cycle stages of a dragonfly (egg, nymph, adult) but does not use a flow chart, which the competency explicitly requires. The content is related to life cycles but does not directly support the skill of using flow charts to compare stages.

copy.en: A dragonfly lays its eggs in water, and its young live underwater as a nymph before climbing out to become a flying dragonfly.
copy.tl: Nangingitlog ang tutubi sa tubig, at ang anak nito ay nabubuhay muna sa ilalim ng tubig bilang nymph bago umahon at maging tutubing lumilipad.
copy.bis: Ang alindahaw mangitlog sa tubig, ug ang anak niini magpuyo una ilalom sa tubig isip nymph una mosaka ug mahimong alindahaw nga molupad.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Mosquito larvae grow in standing water
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use flow charts to compare the different stages in the life cycle of animals, such as a butterfly, frog, chicken, and human
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions mosquito larvae but does not compare life-cycle stages or use a flow chart. It focuses on control by removing standing water, not on the stages of the mosquito life cycle.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the best way to fight mosquitoes is to empty out old tires, cans, and other containers that collect water around the house
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that there is a need to protect and conserve the environment for living things to survive
assignedReviews.reason: The card suggests an environmental action (removing containers) but does not teach the need to protect and conserve the environment for living things to survive. It is about pest control, not conservation or protection of the environment for survival.

copy.en: Mosquito larvae grow in standing water, so the best way to fight mosquitoes is to empty out old tires, cans, and other containers that collect water around the house.
copy.tl: Nabubuhay ang mga uod ng lamok sa nakatayong tubig, kaya ang pinakamagandang paraan para makontrol ang lamok ay ang pag-aalis ng mga lalagyan ng tubig tulad ng lumang gulong at lata sa paligid ng bahay.
copy.bis: Ang mga ulod sa lamok nagpuyo sa nagtindog nga tubig, mao nga ang labing maayong paagi sa pagkontrol sa lamok mao ang pagtangtang sa mga sudlanan sa tubig sama sa daang gulong ug lata palibot sa balay.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A tunicate larva has a brain-like structure and notochord, but during metamorphosis it attaches to a surface and reabsorbs its own brain and notochord
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the differences between animals with a backbone (vertebrates) and animals without backbones (invertebrates) by using common local examples of each group
assignedReviews.reason: A larval notochord is not the Grade 6 difference between animals with a backbone and animals without backbones.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: during metamorphosis it attaches to a surface and reabsorbs its own brain and notochord
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use flow charts to compare the different stages in the life cycle of animals, such as a butterfly, frog, chicken, and human
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not use flow charts to compare life-cycle stages of a butterfly, frog, chicken, and human.

copy.en:
What happens to a tunicate's brain?

A tunicate larva has a brain-like structure and notochord, but during metamorphosis it attaches to a surface and reabsorbs its own brain and notochord!
copy.tl:
Ano ang nangyayari sa utak ng tunicate?

May katulad-utak na istruktura at notochord ang larva ng tunicate, pero sa metamorphosis, dumidikit ito at sinisipsip muli ang sarili nitong utak at notochord!
copy.bis:
Unsay mahitabo sa utok sa tunicate?

Ang larva sa tunicate adunay istruktura nga sama sa utok ug notochord, apan sa metamorphosis, kini modikit ug mo-absorb balik sa iyang kaugalingong utok ug notochord!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: both are forms of energy that travel in waves
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain in terms of the particle model the processes underlying convection and conduction of heat energy
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses light and sound as forms of energy traveling in waves. It does not address the particle model or the processes of convection and conduction of heat energy, so it provides no direct instructional support for this competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: both are forms of energy that travel in waves
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify advantageous and disadvantageous examples of conduction, convection, and radiation
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about light and sound energy, not about conduction, convection, or radiation, nor about advantageous or disadvantageous examples of these heat transfer modes. It shares only the broad topic of energy and provides no direct support for this competency.

copy.en: Light and sound are similar because both are forms of energy that travel in waves.
copy.tl: Ang liwanag at tunog ay magkatulad dahil pareho silang mga anyo ng enerhiya na naglalakbay sa pamamagitan ng waves.
copy.bis: Ang kahayag ug tingog managsama tungod kay pareho silang mga matang sa enerhiya nga mobiyahe pinaagi sa mga waves.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Light from the Moon takes only about 1.3 seconds to reach the Earth!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: examine a local weather chart to make simple interpretations about the local weather and describe and practice safety precautions to use during poor or extreme weather conditions
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about light travel time from the Moon to Earth. It has no connection to weather charts, weather interpretation, or safety precautions for poor/extreme weather.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Light from the Moon takes only about 1.3 seconds to reach the Earth!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that how far an object moves in a given time is called speed

copy.bis: Ang light-year sukod sa gilay-on, dili oras! Mao kini ang kalayo nga mabaktas sa kahayag sulod sa usa ka tuig — mga 9.5 ka trilyon nga kilometro.

How wide is our Milky Way galaxy?

Our Milky Way is about 100,000 light-years wide! That makes it truly enormous to cross.
copy.tl:
Gaano kalapad ang ating Milky Way?

Ang Milky Way ay tinatayang 100,000 taong-liwanag ang lapad! Kaya napakalaki nito para tawirin.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang gilapdon sa atong Milky Way?

Ang Milky Way mga 100,000 ka tuig-kahayag ang gilapdon! Busa dako kaayo kini aron tabukon.

copy.bis: Kung kalit nga mobarog ang imong buhok ug morag naay nagkiliti sa panit samtang naay bagyo, hapit na moigo ang kilat! Daliana og pungko ug himoa ang lawas nga gamay.

copy.en: Even inside your house during a storm, stay in the middle room! Keep away from windows and doors because electricity can travel through their metal parts.
copy.tl: Kahit nasa loob ka ng bahay habang may bagyo, manatili sa gitnang silid! Lumayo sa bintana at pinto dahil ang kuryente ay pwedeng dumaan sa metal parts.
copy.bis: Bisan nasa sulod ka sa balay samtang naay bagyo, pabilin sa tunga nga lawak! Palayo sa bintana ug pultahan kay ang kuryente moagi sa metal parts.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Lightning is a giant spark of electricity!

copy.en: Lightning is a giant spark of electricity! It jumps between clouds or zaps down from a cloud to the ground.
copy.tl: Ang kidlat ay isang napakalaking kislap ng kuryente! Lumilipad ito sa pagitan ng mga ulap o mula sa ulap papunta sa lupa.
copy.bis: Ang kilat usa ka dako kaayo nga kisaw sa kuryente! Molukso kini tali sa mga panganod o gikan sa panganod paingon sa yuta.

copy.tl: Nilalagyan ng metal na lightning rod ang matataas na gusali! Ginagabayan nito ang kuryente ng kidlat papunta sa lupa nang ligtas para hindi masira ang gusali.
copy.bis: Ang taas nga mga building gibutangan og metal nga lightning rod! Giniyahan niini ang kuryente sa kilat paubos sa yuta nga luwas aron dili madaot ang building.

copy.en: A metal lightning rod on the roof gives lightning a safe path to the ground, keeping the building safe from damage!
copy.tl: Ang metal na lightning rod sa bubong ay nagbibigay ng ligtas na daan sa lupa, kaya hindi nasisira ang gusali!
copy.bis: Ang puthaw nga lightning rod sa atop naghatag og luwas nga dalan paingon sa yuta, aron dili madaot ang building!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The metal shell carries electricity around you and into the ground.

copy.en: Think rubber tires protect you in a car during lightning? Wrong! The metal shell carries electricity around you and into the ground. The metal body keeps you safe, not the tires!
copy.tl: Akala mo ligtas ka sa kotse dahil sa goma ng gulong? Mali! Ang metal na balat ang nagdadala ng kuryente paligid mo at sa lupa. Ang metal ang nagpoprotekta, hindi ang gulong!
copy.bis: Naghunahuna ka nga luwas ka sa sakyanan tungod sa goma sa ligid? Sayop! Ang metal nga panit ang modala sa kuryente palibot nimo ug sa yuta. Ang metal ang mopanalipod, dili ang ligid!

Who was the very first Filipina to be named a National Scientist?

Clara Lim-Sylianco made history in 1994 as the first Filipina woman to be named a National Scientist of the Philippines!
copy.tl:
Sino ang unang babaeng Pilipina na ginawarang Pambansang Siyentista?

Si Clara Lim-Sylianco ang gumawa ng kasaysayan noong 1994 bilang unang babaeng Pilipina na ginawarang Pambansang Siyentista ng Pilipinas!
copy.bis:
Kinsa ang unang babaeng Pilipina nga gihatagan sa titulo nga National Scientist?

Si Clara Lim-Sylianco ang naghimo sa kasaysayan niadtong 1994 isip unang babaeng Pilipina nga gihatagan sa titulo nga National Scientist sa Pilipinas!

Did you know rocks can come from the sea?

Yes! Limestone formed long ago from the shells and coral of sea creatures.

Alam mo bang ang bato ay pwedeng galing sa dagat?

Oo! Ang limestone ay nabuo noong unang panahon mula sa mga kabibe at coral ng mga hayop-dagat.
copy.bis:
Nahibaw-an ba ka nga ang bato pwede gikan sa dagat?

Oo! Ang limestone naporma kaniadto gikan sa mga kabhang ug coral sa mga mananap sa dagat.

assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a rock type but does not involve exploring, observing, collecting, or describing rock features such as texture, color, or grain crystal size.

copy.en: Limestone is a cool sedimentary rock! It forms from piled-up shells and coral on the sea floor, just like the rocks found in Bohol.
copy.tl: Ang limestone ay isang sedimentary na bato! Nabuo ito mula sa naipong mga kabibe at korales sa ilalim ng dagat, tulad ng mga bato sa Bohol.
copy.bis: Ang limestone usa ka sedimentary nga bato! Nabuhat kini gikan sa natipon nga mga kabhang ug coral sa ilawom sa dagat, sama sa mga bato sa Bohol.

Can animals predict when an earthquake is coming?

Even if they act strangely sometimes, there is no sure way for animals to predict an earthquake!

Nakahahula ba ang mga hayop kung kailan darating ang lindol?

Kahit kakaiba minsan ang kilos nila, walang siguradong paraan ang mga hayop para mahulaan ang lindol!

Makatagna ba ang mga mananap kung kanus-a moabot ang linog?

Bisan lahi usahay ang ilang lihok, walay sigurado nga paagi ang mga mananap aron matagna ang linog!

copy.bis: Ang linog mao ang kalit nga pag-uyog sa yuta nga tungod sa paglihok sa mga bato ilalom!

Carl Linnaeus was the scientist who created the modern way of naming living things.

Sino ang gumawa ng paraan sa pagbibigay-pangalan sa mga buhay na bagay?

Si Carl Linnaeus ang siyentipikong gumawa ng modernong paraan ng pagbibigay ng pangalan sa mga buhay na bagay.
copy.bis:
Kinsa ang naghimo sa paagi sa pagngalan sa mga buhing butang?

Si Carl Linnaeus ang siyentista nga naghimo sa modernong paagi sa pagngalan sa mga buhing butang.

What makes a lionfish dangerous to touch?

The lionfish has long spines packed with venom that it uses to defend itself from threats.

Bakit delikado ang lionfish kung mahawakan?

Ang lionfish ay may mahahabang tinik na puno ng lason na ginagamit nito para ipagtanggol ang sarili.
copy.bis:
Nganong peligro hikapon ang lionfish?

Ang lionfish adunay tag-as nga mga tunok nga puno sa hilo nga gigamit niini sa pagpanalipod sa kaugalingon.

What breaks down medicine in your body?

The liver usually breaks down medicine after it has done its job — that's why medicines have a proper dose, so the liver isn't overwhelmed.
copy.tl:
Ano ang sumisira ng gamot sa katawan?

Ang atay ang karaniwang sumisira sa gamot pagkatapos itong gumana — kaya may tamang dosis ang gamot, para hindi mahirapan ang atay.
copy.bis:
Unsay moguba sa tambal sa lawas?

assignedReviews.reason: The card is about tool use to obtain food, not about observing or describing outer body parts (head, legs, wings) and their role in movement or food gathering. It shares the broad topic of animals gathering food but does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: This clever monkey can use stones to crack open shellfish
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a behavior (tool use) but does not describe how an animal has changed to better suit its environment, such as mimicry or camouflage. It does not provide information about evolutionary adaptation or environmental change, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
Which monkey uses stones as tools?

This clever monkey can use stones to crack open shellfish — smart enough to make its own tools for a tasty meal!
copy.tl:
Anong unggoy ang gumagamit ng bato bilang kasangkapan?

Napakatalino ng unggoy na ito at kaya nitong gumamit ng bato para buksan ang mga kabibe — parang may sariling kasangkapan para sa masarap na pagkain!
copy.bis:
Unsa nga unggoy ang mogamit ug bato isip himan?

Kini nga unggoy maalamon kaayo ug makahimong mogamit ug bato aron ablihan ang mga kinhason — daw naay kaugalingong himan para sa lamian nga pagkaon!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Mach 1 means traveling at the speed of sound, which is about 1,235 kilometers per hour!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that how far an object moves in a given time is called speed
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a specific speed (Mach 1 = speed of sound) but does not teach the concept that speed is how far an object moves in a given time. It uses the word 'speed' but provides no instructional support for identifying the definition of speed.

copy.en: Mach 1 means traveling at the speed of sound, which is about 1,235 kilometers per hour!
copy.tl: Ang Mach 1 ay nangangahulugang lumilipad nang kasimbilis ng tunog, mga 1,235 kilometro kada oras!
copy.bis: Ang Mach 1 nagpasabot nga naglupad sa katulin sa tingog, mga 1,235 ka kilometro kada oras!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: With almost no friction, it can run extremely fast and quietly.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate how friction can produce heat and investigate ways of reducing and increasing friction
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions that maglev trains have almost no friction because they have no wheels touching the rail, which is an example of reducing friction. However, it does not demonstrate how friction produces heat nor investigate ways of reducing and increasing friction as required by the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A maglev train has no wheels touching the rail!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify examples of how objects can affect other objects even when they are not in contact with each other, such as magnets attracting other objects, light from the sun, and loud noises hurting our ears
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a maglev train, which uses magnets to levitate, but it does not identify examples of how objects affect other objects without contact. It only states that there are no wheels touching the rail, without explaining the magnetic non-contact force or giving other examples like magnets attracting objects.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A maglev train has no wheels touching the rail!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a simple electromagnet and observe and record its properties
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not mention electromagnets, making one, or observing/recording properties. Maglev trains may use electromagnets, but the card only discusses friction and speed, not electromagnet construction or properties.

copy.en:
How does a maglev train run so fast?

A maglev train has no wheels touching the rail! With almost no friction, it can run extremely fast and quietly.
copy.tl:
Paano tumatakbo nang napakabilis ang maglev train?

Ang maglev train ay walang gulong na dumidikit sa riles! Dahil halos walang friction, tumatakbo ito nang napakabilis at tahimik.
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagdagan nga paspas kaayo ang maglev train?

Ang maglev train walay ligid nga modikit sa riles! Tungod kay halos walay friction, makadagan kini nga paspas kaayo ug hilom.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The Earth acts like a giant magnet with its own magnetic field surrounding it.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out guided investigations to identify the properties of magnets, including how they affect other magnets and objects made of different materials
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that Earth behaves like a giant magnet with a magnetic field. It does not describe properties of magnets (e.g., poles, attraction/repulsion) or how magnets affect other magnets and objects made of different materials, which is the focus of G4-F-7.

copy.en:
Is the Earth actually a giant magnet?

Yes! The Earth acts like a giant magnet with its own magnetic field surrounding it.
copy.tl:
Ang Mundo ba ay isang malaking magnet?

Oo! Ang Mundo ay parang malaking magnet na may sariling magnetic field na pumapalibot dito.
copy.bis:
Ang Kalibotan ba usa ka dako nga magnet?

Oo! Ang Kalibotan sama sa dakong magnet, nga adunay kaugalingong magnetic field nga naglibot niini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: an electromagnet only works while electricity flows through it
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a simple electromagnet and observe and record its properties
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states a property of an electromagnet (works only with electricity) and compares it to a permanent magnet. It does not teach how to make a simple electromagnet, nor does it guide observing and recording its properties as required by the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A permanent magnet, like your fridge magnet, is always magnetic without electricity
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out guided investigations to identify the properties of magnets, including how they affect other magnets and objects made of different materials
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a permanent magnet and its property of being always magnetic, but it does not address investigating how magnets affect other magnets or objects made of different materials, which is the core of the competency.

copy.en: A permanent magnet, like your fridge magnet, is always magnetic without electricity. But an electromagnet only works while electricity flows through it. That’s their main difference!
copy.tl: Ang permanent magnet, tulad ng sa ref, ay laging magnetic kahit walang kuryente. Pero ang electromagnet ay nagiging magnet lang kapag may dumadaloy na kuryente. Iyan ang pagkakaiba nila!
copy.bis: Ang permanent magnet, sama sa sa ref, kanunay nga magnetic bisan walay kuryente. Pero ang electromagnet mahimong magnet lamang kung adunay nag-agos nga kuryente. Mao kana ang ilang kalainan!
